findings.explanation: The module generates an SSH keypair (tls_private_key.ssh), writes the private key to a local plaintext file, and pushes the public key into project metadata under the key "ssh-keys2". This has no effect for two independent reasons: (1) the GCE guest agent only reads the literal metadata key "ssh-keys" (or legacy "sshKeys") for key-based SSH — a custom key name like "ssh-keys2" is never consulted, and (2) the instance sets metadata `enable-oslogin = "TRUE"` (google_compute_instance.vm_instance.tf:27), which makes GCE ignore metadata SSH keys entirely in favor of IAM-based OS Login. An operator who pulls the generated id_rsa private key expecting it to authenticate will find it does nothing, which is confusing during an access/incident scenario and represents wasted resources (key generation, project-metadata write, local plaintext key file) for a feature that is dead on arrival.
findings.remediation: Pick one consistent access model: either drop the tls_private_key/local_file/google_compute_project_metadata_item resources entirely and rely on OS Login (already enabled) with IAM role bindings for SSH, or if metadata-key SSH is actually wanted, remove `enable-oslogin` and rename the metadata key from "ssh-keys2" to the instance-level "ssh-keys" metadata block (scoped to the instance, not the whole project) so GCE actually honors it.
findings.title: Generated SSH keypair is provisioned but can never be used to log in

findings.explanation: The module uses the google, tls, and local providers but declares no `terraform { required_providers { ... } }` block anywhere at the root (main.tf is just a stray comment). Only the example/examplea consumer pins a google provider version. Without constraints, consumers can pick up breaking provider releases silently, and the module's own behavior isn't reproducible across environments or CI runs.
findings.remediation: Add a terraform.tf (or extend main.tf) at the module root with a required_providers block pinning google, tls, and local to compatible version ranges, plus a required_version for the Terraform CLI.
findings.title: Root module has no required_providers / required_version constraints

findings.explanation: outputs.tf exists but is completely empty. The module creates a compute instance, an SSH keypair, and project metadata, but exposes none of it (instance name/self_link/id, network IP, or the generated public key). Consumers can't reference the created instance without reaching into the module's internal resource addresses via workarounds, which defeats module encapsulation.
findings.remediation: Add outputs for at least the instance's id/self_link and network_interface IP so callers can compose with the module output instead of guessing internal resource names.
findings.title: Module exposes zero outputs

findings.explanation: local_file.private and local_file.public write to the fixed relative paths "id_rsa" and "id_rsa.pub" in the working directory. If this module is instantiated more than once from the same root config (e.g. for two instances/environments), both instantiations resolve to the same on-disk path and silently overwrite each other's key files, so whichever apply ran last wins with no warning.
findings.remediation: Parameterize the output filename (e.g. include var.username or a caller-supplied prefix) or accept an output directory/path variable so multiple module instances in the same working directory don't collide.
findings.title: Generated SSH key files use a hardcoded, non-namespaced filename

findings.explanation: description = "I think you'll figure this one out" is a placeholder, not real documentation. Generated module docs (terraform-docs, registry pages) will surface this text verbatim to consumers.
findings.fix: description = "The Linux username to provision on the instance and register with the generated SSH keypair."
findings.remediation: Replace with a real description, e.g. "The Linux username to provision on the instance and register with the generated SSH keypair."
findings.title: variable "username" has a joke placeholder description
